text:
acme-platform: Anyone awake? We're seeing browsers get SSE events for ~180-300 tokens then the stream closes unexpectedly. This started after we rolled Envoy 1.28 at the edge. We proxy browser->HAProxy->Cloudflare->our Envoy->Redwood. Clients report duplicate tokens on reconnect and we're getting sudden billing spikes.
acme-platform: Here's an example server-side request to Redwood (we use HTTP/2 to the API):

```
curl -v --http2-prior-knowledge \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  -H \"User-Agent: acme-proxy/2.0\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses -d '{"input":"please stream me many tokens"}'
```

acme-platform: Direct curl to api.redwood.ai from our CI (no Cloudflare/HAProxy) returns continuous SSE until completion. Full chain returns first ~220 tokens then our HAProxy logs show BUFFER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and Envoy logs show upstream FIN then downstream RST_STREAM.

acme-platform: Attaching a small tcpdump snippet (timestamps relative):
```
1858012357 send chunk (token stream)
1858012360 upstream FIN from Envoy->Redwood path
1858012361 downstream RST_STREAM to client
```

acme-platform: Also notice when client reconnects we get a fresh billed request ID on Redwood (tokens counted twice). Can Redwood dedupe resumed requests? We're not intentionally reissuing same prompt, just reconnecting.
aisha (Support): Sorry for the trouble. Quick answers: 1) We don't currently support transparent resume semantics server-side; each new connection is billed independently. 2) We can add more debug logging if you append `x-redwood-debug: true` to requests. 3) Did you confirm whether the intermediary rewrites `Transfer-Encoding` or adds `Content-Length`? That typically turns an otherwise streaming response into a buffered one.

acme-platform: We captured headers: at HAProxy exit we saw `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, but after Cloudflare it sometimes becomes `Content-Length: 912` mid-response. That forces buffering until complete and then a burst close. Some runs show Cloudflare rewriting when it detects many small flushes; other runs show HAProxy tripping a buffer limit.

jordan (SRE): @leo can you check if our runtime/ingress is emitting any abnormal window updates or resetting streams around that timeframe? If the runtime sends small, frequent frames and the gateway aggregates them, proxy buffer limits get hit. Also we need to search logs for `client_closed_request` or `RST_STREAM` for the incoming connection timestamps 1858012357-1858012400.

leo (Infra): Noted. Envoy 1.28 introduced changes in the buffer filter and http2 flow control defaults; we've seen cases where intermediaries holding chunked responses until a content-length is computed cause early FIN/RST. Two likely failure modes: 1) proxy buffers until reaching its max buffer and then errors; 2) translator proxies (gRPC->HTTP1) set `content-length` incorrectly when trailers arrive and then close stream. Both result in abrupt client disconnects and duplicate reconnects.

ben (SDK): Short-term mitigation for customers: 1) Ask them to use direct HTTP/2 to Redwood (bypass Cloudflare) or pin to our Dedicated peered endpoints for heavy streaming. 2) If they must go through proxies, suggest disabling proxy buffering and preserving `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` or end-to-end HTTP/2 prior knowledge. We can also provide a header `x-redwood-connection-id` as the first SSE event so clients can correlate reconnections and perform client-side dedupe for billing.

acme-platform: Client-side dedupe would help. But if the reconnect results in partial duplicate tokens mid-sentence, client-side heuristics may be tricky. Any plan from Redwood to avoid double-billing when reconnects are provably proxy-caused?
aisha (Support): For billing we can entertain credits on a case-by-case basis if logs show proxy-induced disconnects. From a product perspective we could do a low-effort improvement: 1) emit `x-redwood-connection-id` (UUID) as the first SSE `event: meta` line, 2) accept `x-redwood-resume: <uuid>` header on reconnects within a short window (e.g., 30s) and mark duplicate tokens as non-billable in our accounting (soft dedupe). Full resume of generation state (KV cache) requires persistent generation sessions and is a larger feature.

leo (Infra): Operational actions: 1) grep Envoy logs for that customer connection id and time range; 2) reproduce with Envoy 1.27 vs 1.28 to confirm regression; 3) check HAProxy buffer thresholds and Cloudflare streaming settings. If HAProxy shows BUFFER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, increase buffers or lower flush chunk sizes.

acme-platform: Could Redwood throttle or change chunking frequency server-side to avoid tripping intermediary buffers? If we flush smaller chunks more often maybe proxies won't accumulate large buffers.
aisha (Support): We can ship an experiment flag to the runtime to increase flush frequency (`flush_interval_ms`/`frequent_flush` feature-flag) so tokens are emitted in smaller, more frequent frames. That might keep intermediaries from hitting their buffer high-water marks. Not a complete fix but could reduce incidents. I'll open a task and wire a feature-flag rollout.

ben (SDK): I'll prototype the `x-redwood-connection-id` echo and have the API include `event: meta\ndata: {"connection_id":"<uuid>"}` as the first SSE chunk. That will let clients correlate and optionally pass `x-redwood-resume` on reconnect. We should document that resume is best-effort and not a real generation state resume.

jordan (SRE): Action list: 
- @acme-platform: run two repros and attach tcpdump + verbose curl for direct vs full-chain attempts
- @leo: check proxy logs and Envoy config for http2 and buffer changes post-1.28
- @ben: prototype `connection_id` echo header/event (non-resumable)
- @aisha: collection of runtime logs for the request ids and flags for billing review

deploy-bot: runtime flag rollout started 2026-03-15T20:10:00Z (target: frequent-flush experiment)

acme-platform: Thanks. We ran the two repros: direct -> stable, full chain -> breaks. HAProxy shows BUFFER_LIMIT_EXCEEDED then Envoy 1.28 returns RST_STREAM after an upstream write. When we retested by disabling HAProxy buffering, the behavior went away. So proxy buffering + chunk aggregation is the root cause for us.

aisha (Support): Good find. Short-term recommendation for you: try to disable buffering at HAProxy/Cloudflare or configure them for streaming (Cloudflare Streamed responses / disable `no_chunked` rewrite). We'll queue the runtime `frequent-flush` flag to help other customers. For billing credits, please DM our billing team with the tcpdump + our debug logs and we'll review.

acme-platform: Appreciate it. We'll try the disable-buffering route and test the frequent-flush flag once available. We'll also watch for any duplicate charges and open a billing ticket if needed. Thanks all.
